Satya Nadella: Windows 10 being free will help Microsoft lure phone developers
Phone developers already have something which is free AND Open Source.

The issues with Windows Phone go far deeper than availability and cross-platform support. The problem is that Microsoft's phone platform feels more restrictive and less capable than alternatives: The main screen isn't as inviting. Settings (such as those that restrict and dictate data usage) are on by default and hidden in menus (sometimes multiple menus). You have less flexibility on how things look and feel and function. Getting to meaningful things is more of a hassle. It's harder to make your device feel like it is your own. Microsoft isn't as upfront and transparent about how apps use your device and information. They want to force people into accepting access to location info in applications when it isn't necessary for core functionality--preventing you from using it at all. There is far less integration of core services and functionality--like voice navigation--and with recent announcements this isn't getting any better. And much more.

Just bringing in developers isn't going to fix these very important issues, and unless Windows 10 has some major, and unannounced, features in the works all of the things Microsoft is talking about are meaningless and futile.

Perhaps they should try sticking to their guns and developing features to maturity rather than selling them off and/or dropping them short of the goal line. It is hurting them in the long run and setting them back when it comes to being able to provide a top-level, integrated, and fully functional platform.

The uniformity that Microsoft have been showing off between desktop and mobile apps in Windows 10 seems very promising. I actually have high hopes that they'll finally pull off what they've been struggling to do for years now, but I fear it is too late. I am a happy Android user, but good on them for keeping at it though.

Aside: Did anyone else get excited to see Nadella mention HoloLens and Windows 10? Makes me think that perhaps we could see HoloLens in 2016 sometime.
